notes:
Account summary: mid-market B2B SaaS (product analytics dashboards) looking to move from Hosted API trial -> Dedicated for production helpdesk/chat + document search. Highly product-minded team; CTO (quote): "We need predictable latency and unit economics — if we can hit ~150ms p95 and stable costs we buy."

Key ask: POC must validate canary + fallback routing across model variants and region failover. They want explicit rollback steps and monitoring hooks (per-model latency and token cost).

Technical details / preferences:
- Primary workload: real-time chat (support agent) with embeddings-backed doc search and occasional reranking for top results.
- Latency target: p95 <= 200ms for chat in NA region; throughput burst ~200 qps during peak.
- Cost sensitivity: mid-market budget, expects Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching) to reduce token spend ~30% without quality regression.
- Model preference: open models with possible Redwood-curated variants; willing to test 8-bit/quantized variants if fidelity checks pass.
- Routing plan desired: canary to model-variant A (high quality) on 5% traffic, fallback to cheaper variant B on overload or region outage, automatic region failover NA->EU for continuity, and manual rollback path.

Operational / security notes:
- Need SSO/SAML for users, audit logging retention 1 year, and integration with customer KMS for key wrapping.
- Data residency: primary NA, legal asks for contract language on ephemeral data retention.

Quotes and shorthand from calls:
- CTO: "We need a safe path to start rolling workloads without blowing up our cloud bill."
- Head of Infra: "Show me the failover runbook and how the KV cache behaves across regions."

Artifacts referenced: pricing deck (drive), security FAQ, two recorded calls (fireflies). Jira tickets for early infra questions.

Next steps (short): finalize SOW, grant VPC peering + KMS test keys, schedule canary runbook review w/ platform engineers, provide sample traffic profile for POC.

Sales notes: good champion in VP Product (referred by existing customer), procurement cycle likely Jan 2026 if POC satisfactory. Keep pricing flexibility around burst capacity.
